claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can be synthesized by powder metallurgy, including spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder.
An equiatomic or near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy provides the proposed baseline state.
A compositional series can be made by incrementally increasing or decreasing selected elemental concentrations while keeping the total elemental fraction constant.
Moderate variations of approximately 5–10% relative to the equiatomic composition are proposed.
Spark plasma sintering can produce fully dense HfNbTaTiZr material.
Spark plasma sintering ensures reproducibility across the compositional series.
Changing elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr modifies lattice distortion.
Changing elemental percentages may alter phase stability, grain size, or secondary-phase formation.
Composition-induced lattice and microstructural changes mediate dislocation motion.
Changing individual elemental percentages adjusts the local bonding environment and solid-solution strengthening.
Changes in local bonding and solid-solution strengthening alter dislocation dynamics.
Altered dislocation dynamics result in changes in hardness and yield strength.
Mechanical properties will vary systematically with elemental composition.
Increasing lattice distortion is expected to enhance strengthening.
The compositional effect should be observable within variations of approximately 5–10% for one element.
Larger compositional variations may cause phase instability or undesirable secondary phases.
Hardness, yield strength, phase constitution, and microstructure can be compared across identically processed samples to test the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a systematic or monotonic mechanical-property trend, or the expected microstructural correlation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis allows element-dependent trends and warns that interactions may preclude a simple monotonic relationship, but the falsification rule treats absence of monotonic variation as falsifying.

The stated range is about ±5–10% relative to an equiatomic composition, whereas the example reduces Hf from 15% to 5%; relative to an equiatomic 20 at.% baseline, this is a substantially larger change.
